description: Canonical behavioral cases for hash-free exact text replacement with an optional section scope. This file is the single source of truth for both exposed adapters: the Memory MCP `replace_in_note` tool and the Autonomy native note-replacement tool (which must run a byte-identical snapshot of this file, recording this file's path and hash as provenance). Every case must be run through the exposed tool adapter (not a shared helper), asserting the exact resulting full-note bytes on success and exact byte-for-byte refusal (no write at all) on failure. Scope uniqueness counts overlapping occurrences; a scoped case matches only inside the resolved section; a batch applies progressively in memory but is validated in full before any write, so any failure leaves the note unchanged.

errorKinds.not-found: an edit's oldText has zero possible matches in the selected scope
errorKinds.ambiguous: an edit's oldText has more than one possible (including overlapping) match in the selected scope
errorKinds.section-not-found: the section path matches zero sections
errorKinds.section-ambiguous: the section path matches more than one section

cases.description: Unscoped replace: oldText occurs exactly once in the whole note; only the matched span changes.
cases.expectedContent:
# Title

first paragraph

second paragraph, edited

cases.description: Unscoped replace where oldText appears nowhere: refuse, bytes unchanged.
Unscoped replace where oldText appears twice: refuse as ambiguous, bytes unchanged.
oldText 'aa' fits at two overlapping positions in 'aaa': ambiguous even though a non-overlapping match count would report one.
Scoped replace: oldText occurs once inside the selected section and once outside it; only the inside occurrence changes and the outside text is untouched.

cases.description: Scoped replace where oldText exists only outside the selected section: refuse with the scoped not-found error, bytes unchanged.
cases.content:

unique haystack text

## B

other body

# A

## B

other body

cases.description: Section path matches zero sections: refuse before validating edits, bytes unchanged.
Section path matches two sections with the same heading: refuse as ambiguous, bytes unchanged.
Batch applies progressively: the second edit's oldText exists only after the first edit's output.
Batch with one valid edit then one unmatchable edit: the whole batch is refused and the note's bytes are untouched (no partial write even though the first edit validated in memory).
Empty oldText 'matches' at every character boundary of non-empty content, so it is ambiguous - preserved historical behavior, not silently widened.
Scoped batch: two edits, each unique inside the selected section; text duplicated elsewhere in the note stays untouched.

shared token inside
more shared token
